timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What's the difference between a monolithic and microkernel?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Monolithic puts everything in kernel space — fast but one bug can compromise everything. Microkernel keeps most things in user space.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Not necessarily less secure, but a single kernel vulnerability has a larger blast radius. Linux is monolithic and very secure.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What about access control? I've heard of DAC and MAC.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: DAC lets owners decide permissions. MAC enforces system-wide policies. RBAC assigns permissions based on roles.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: There is no 'best.' MAC is strictest — used in military. DAC is most common. Most systems use a combination.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What about ASLR and DEP? Those sound technical.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: ASLR randomizes where code loads in memory. DEP prevents executing data. Both make exploitation much harder.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Do all operating systems have these?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Modern ones do. But older systems or embedded devices often skip them for performance or compatibility.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So the OS I choose actually matters for security?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Enormously. The OS is the foundation. A weak foundation means every other control is compromised.
